subject: Re: VeloxData demo — streaming duplication observed
messages:

Subject: VeloxData demo — streaming duplication observed

Marcus / Logan —

Quick summary from this morning's Velox demo (Alex on the thread): during a 30-user live session they saw duplicate final "done"/completion tokens emitted to the client after a short network glitch. The app showed duplicated message cards and the customer got confused mid-demo. I recorded their screen (attached) and pulled logs (attached zip).

What we observed:
- SDK: JS SDK v1.14.0 (they updated last week)
- Event sequence in logs: STREAM_OPEN -> partial events -> NETWORK_TIMEOUT -> RECONNECT -> duplicate FINAL_EVENT (same content, same request id)
- Duplicate final event arrives ~200ms after the original final event

Ask: can platform/runtime confirm whether this is a runtime duplicate emission (same token re-sent) or an SDK delivery/ack race? Customer is evaluating for production next month; they'd like a mitigation/temporary workaround.

Attaching: velox_demo_logs.zip, screencap-duplication.mp4

Thanks — can we triage fast? I can organize a short RCA call with Alex tomorrow afternoon.

—Sean
Senior Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the write-up and the attachments, Sean. I skimmed the logs in the zip — good signal. A few quick clarifying questions before I pull runtime traces:

1) Does the duplicated final event show the same request-id/stream-id and identical token sequence? If so, that strongly points to a delivery duplicate rather than application-level dedupe.
2) Can you confirm whether Velox is using the SDK's automatic reconnect (default) or a custom reconnect/backoff implementation? The SDK introduced a reconnect race in 1.14 where the reconnect handshake can complete while the previous stream still flushes the final chunk in some edge timing cases.

Immediate asks from runtime side: if you can extract a small repro that reproduces in a few seconds (curl or a simple JS script) and paste it here, we can run it against a canary to validate. If it's clearly the SDK reconnect race, the short-term mitigation is to increase reconnect backoff and add an idempotency header on streaming finalization so runtime can dedupe by request-id.

I'll open a Jira with what I have and loop infra to see if we can instrument the emitter path to add an ephemeral de-dup filter. If you can run a short curl test (I give steps below) and confirm the phenomenon that would help prioritize.

Curl repro (quick):
- Start a streaming request with ?stream=true and X-Request-Id header
- Drop the connection after partial tokens (tcpkill / network drop)
- Reopen within 1s and observe final tokens (we expect a single final token; if duplicate, send the two raw frames)

I'll try to get traces from the canary by EOD.

—Marcus
Principal Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

Sean / Marcus —

Quick field workaround that has helped a couple of customers recently:
- Client: set STREAM_RECONNECT_BACKOFF_MS to 1500 (was default 300ms)
- Client: include X-Stream-Id and X-Stream-Id-Checksum headers (SDK can be toggled to emit these)
- Platform: runtime can honor X-Stream-Id and suppress duplicate final frames within a 5s sliding window per stream id

Short-term we can ask runtime to push a canary filter that drops duplicate final frames where Request-Id and final token hash match within 5s. We call this the "final-dedupe" guard — non-invasive, canaryable, and cheap to revert. Longer-term we should fix the SDK handshake ordering.

If Marcus is OK to open the canary, we can coordinate with Velox for a short window tomorrow morning to validate. That gives the sales team something to show while infra lands a proper fix.

—Logan
Director, Sales Engineering

Thanks, Logan. I'll scope the canary. Plan below:
1) INF-9876: create a short-lived middleware in front of emitter that dedupes final frames by (request-id, final-token-hash) for a 72-hour canary window. No model changes.
2) Instrument telemetry metric dedupe.final.count and add an alert if rate > 0.1% of streaming sessions in canary (to detect unintended suppression).
3) Push canary to a small subset of hosts tonight (estimate: 4 hours) and open a rollback path to revert within 30 minutes if we see regression.

Sean — please run the curl repro and the client workaround (increase backoff) against our canary once it's up and paste the raw frames so I can validate. Alex — if you can spare one hour tomorrow morning we can run an A/B with and without the canary to confirm behaviour.

I'll link the canary deployment and the INF ticket once created.

—Marcus
